mcat_description.short: Mobile Cabins are relocatable, prefabricated steel-frame structures designed for temporary or semi-permanent use as site offices, guard rooms, labour accommodation, and storage units on construction and industrial sites. They are sold per unit or per square foot, manufactured from mild steel frames with sandwich panel or corrugated sheet walls, and can be transported and reinstalled without structural damage.
mcat_description.long: Mobile Cabins are factory-built, self-contained portable structures constructed on a mild steel base frame with corrugated MS or colour-coated GI/sandwich panel walls, insulated roofs, and fitted doors and windows — designed for rapid deployment and relocation across project sites. In the Indian B2B market, they serve as construction site offices, security guard rooms, worker bunk houses, canteens, and temporary storage units for infrastructure, mining, solar, and industrial projects. Standard commercial sizes range from 6×4 ft (guard cabins) to 40×10 ft (container-style site offices), with insulation options including EPS thermocol, glasswool, and PUF panels to suit varying climate conditions. Buyers typically procure per unit for standard catalogue sizes or negotiate per square foot for custom-dimension builds, with customisation covering size, colour, door/window placement, electrical fittings, and sanitary provisions.

market_context: Mobile Cabins in the Indian market are prefabricated, relocatable structures built on mild steel frames with corrugated MS or colour-coated GI/sandwich panel walls, sold primarily for construction site offices, security guard rooms, and labour accommodation. The dominant structural material is mild steel (MS), with wall panel options including PUF sandwich panels, glasswool-insulated GI sheets, EPS thermocol panels, FRP, ACP, and cement fibre board — each suited to different insulation and durability requirements. Standard commercial sizes follow a modular logic: 10×8 ft (guard cabins), 20×10 ft (site offices), and 40×10 ft (container-style offices) are the most commonly traded dimensions, with custom sizes available from 4×4 ft to 60×15 ft. The term 'Porta Cabin' is the most widely used trade synonym in India; 'Container Cabin' and 'Trolley Cabin' are used specifically for wheel/skid-mounted mobile variants. Tata Steel's MobiNest is the most prominent branded product in this category, confirming steel-frame construction as the dominant commercial form. Buyers in construction, mining, solar, and infrastructure sectors are the primary demand drivers; rental/leasing of cabins is also an active sub-market. Units are quoted per piece for standard sizes and per square foot for custom builds. No single BIS/IS standard governs the entire category, though structural steel and panel materials are subject to relevant IS standards.
